title: 2026-10-22_Mirai_Botnet_Investigation_17e
description: Investigate and mitigate Mirai botnet activity within the sandbox environment.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and performance degradation. Your task is to investigate and identify the source of these issues.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano
Enter 'start' to begin.
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Use the provided credentials (Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano) and enter 'start' to begin.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that communicates with an external host?
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services. The service name should be 'bot-beacon.service'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services.

levels.title: Identify Network Flooding Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service that is generating high volumes of network traffic?
levels.solution: Examine the systemd services and look for any services that might be responsible for network flooding. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services. The service name should be 'bot-flood.service'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd services and look for any services that might be responsible for network flooding.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service?
levels.solution: Investigate the systemd timers and look for any timers associated with the suspicious service. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers. The persistence mechanism should be 'systemd timer'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate the systemd timers and look for any timers associated with the suspicious service.
